_comment: CASTING, NOT PROSE.
The words live in scripts/game/Story.gd, which is canon and is checked
against docs/STORY.md by tools/storytest.gd. This file says WHO SPEAKS
THEM. An earlier version of this file carried its own copy of the
narration, written before Story.gd existed, and the two had already
drifted into contradicting each other: it invented a sworn 'order' that
sent the player, where canon is explicit that the walker is any of 139
champions and may not be named or characterised at all. Two sources of
prose is not a redundancy, it is a bug with a delay on it.
A BEAT IS A SPEAKING ROLE, NOT A VOICE. Recasting the narrator, or
slowing it down, is one edit here. No call site names a voice, a speed or
a volume: they call Narration.say_story('act_open', act) and nothing more.
`story` casts every beat Story.gd advertises, and says how that beat's
lines are named on disk and how they are indexed. Every beat in
Story.beats() MUST appear here — scripts/game/Narration.gd pushes an
error for one that does not, and tools/voicetest.gd fails on it, because
a beat that quietly goes unvoiced is exactly the kind of hole nothing
else in the project would notice.
key   — the wav's filename, printf-style. FORMATTED BY BOTH HALVES of
the pipeline (Narration.gd to find a line's audio, and
tools/gen_voice.py by way of Narration), and %02d means the
same thing in GDScript and in Python, so one pattern here
cannot disagree with itself about where a line lives.
index — how the beat is enumerated:
act_line  one wav per line per act   (act, ordinal)
act       one wav per act            (act)
map       one wav per flavoured map  (map index)
once      a single wav               (no arguments)
KEYS ARE FILENAMES — assets/voice/<key>.wav — so [a-z0-9_] only. A key
with a space or a slash in it renders to a path nothing can load back,
and the symptom is a silent line rather than an error.
`lines` is for the few utility lines Story.gd does not cover: board and
bookkeeping chatter, which is not story and does not belong in the story
module. Their text does live here, because here is its only home.

narrator.note: British, graver, slow. The road itself, not a person in it.

boss.note: A champion who got here first and stayed. Louder than the narrator on purpose: it is in the room with you.

herald.note: Board and reward chatter. Sits under everything — bookkeeping, not drama.

boss_near.text: Something ahead of you walked this road before you did, and stopped here.

champion_down.text: Down. The road does not mind, and it does not wait.

tier_cleared.text: A hundred maps behind you, and the gate at the end of them opens onto the first one again.

quest_offered.text: A reason to go back. Take it, or leave it on the board for somebody else.

quest_paid.text: Paid, and recorded. The board has more where that came from.
